paragraphs: Julota sells a platform that gives emergency responders, clinical practitioners and case workers the same longitudinal view of an individual's history. The company says it makes existing software systems interoperable without new hardware, with data, workflows and reports reached through any browser. Consent management is part of the platform, and Julota states that it is HIPAA and 42CFR compliant. Programs listed as users include crisis intervention teams and community response teams.

Co-founder Rick Pionkowski, an ER doctor at Penrose Hospital in Colorado Springs, saw a disconnected system of community providers produce repeat low-acuity patients at the ER. The first client was the Colorado Springs Fire Department and its Mobile Integrated Healthcare program, CARES. Law enforcement behavioral health followed with the El Paso County Sheriffs office and its Crisis Response Team program.

Julota says it supports co-responder programs across the state of Washington and won its first state contract with the State of Idaho Department of Behavioral Health. It was later selected as the platform for the Southwest Texas Regional Advisory Council, as designated by the Texas Department of State Health Services.

quote.text: Julota transforms the disconnected patchwork of local service providers into a well-coordinated network that serves the community efficiently.
